# `assess` command

Run ensembles of variants of a case and report what their spread says about the accuracy of its quantities.

```bash
fobis assess CASE [options]
```

How to use it, with examples: [Verifying results](/cookbook/verification).

<!-- cli:begin -->
<!-- generated by docs/scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from the command line: do not edit -->

## All options

Arguments: `NAME`

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fobos`, `-f` | TEXT |  | Specify a "fobos" file named differently from "fobos" |
| `--fci` |  |  | Assume fobos inputs as case insensitive |
| `--mode` | TEXT |  | Select a mode defined into a fobos file |
| `--families` | TEXT |  | Comma-separated: precision, rounding, compiler, parallel, inputs, refinement [default: the case's [assess:NAME] families, else rounding]. |
| `--samples` | INTEGER |  | Monte Carlo samples of the inputs family. |
| `--jobs`, `-j` | INTEGER | `1` | Runs at a time (builds are sequential). |
| `--runner` | TEXT | `local` | Where the programs run: local, or slurm (jobs submitted with sbatch; [scheduler] settings). |
| `--json` |  |  | Emit structured JSON to stdout instead of human-readable output (useful for scripting / agents) |

<!-- cli:end -->
